newsitem.title: USA: CS First Boston says SEC action must be dismissed.
newsitem.headline: CS First Boston says SEC action must be dismissed.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston Corp asked a federal court in California to dismiss the Securities and Exchange Commission's suit against the firm for alleged fraud in the sale of Orange County, Calif., bonds, the firm's attorneys said Tuesday.

In court papers filed in U.S. District Court in Santa Ana, Credit Suisse First Boston, an affiliate of CS Holding, denied the SEC's allegations and argued that the complaint must be dismissed because the firm "complied fully with all standards of the securities industry in connection with the pension bond underwriting."
In November, the SEC sued Credit Suisse First Boston Corp, alleging fraud in the sale of $110 million of Series B pension obligation bonds issued by Orange County in September 1994.

Credit Suisse First Boston was the senior underwriter of the pension bonds. SEC alleged that the official statement for the bonds misrepresented and omitted several material facts about the county's investments.

In its response to the SEC allegations, Credit Suisse First Boston said the complaint should be dismissed because the firm was not obligated to verify certain information provided by the county for use in the official statement.
